primary_decision: maximum residue recall at empirical precision >=0.90 with >=50 TP and exact score ties
guardrail: no-linker-protein specificity loss <=0.02 absolute versus weighted-BCE 0.971631

first_trial.hypothesis: Bidirectional sequence context in a dedicated linker head improves high-precision DLD linker recall over the frozen ESM-2 35M residue CNN
first_trial.expected_failure: DLD training labels may not contain sufficient signal; the BiLSTM may overfit or underperform at high precision
first_trial.adaptation: Use the same frozen ESM-2 35M embeddings, DLD folds, and binary labels as our CNN reference. This tests the sequence-context head, not the paper's ProtT5 backbone or multi-task task formulation.

second_trial.hypothesis: A wider bidirectional receptive field from dilated residual convolutions improves high-precision DLD linker recall over the shallow residue CNN without recurrent overfitting
second_trial.expected_failure: Wider context may suppress confident short linkers or increase high-scoring loop false positives, yielding no >=0.90 precision operating point
second_trial.adaptation: Noncausal symmetric protein-residue context rather than the paper's causal temporal sequence model; frozen ESM-2 35M embeddings and unchanged DLD binary labels
second_trial.loss: weighted BCE, positive weight 6, no boundary or minimum-span decoder

selection: No minimum-span decoder for the architecture-only comparison; combine only after an independently useful head result. Do not retune length 4 on fold 4.
next_evidence: Build a homology-audited, separately adjudicated test source before any generalization claim. DisProt may overlap DLD and is not automatically independent.
